newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Canadian miner fears red tape may tie up Czech gold.
newsitem.headline: Canadian miner fears red tape may tie up Czech gold.

text.p: Canadian mining company TVX Gold Inc. said Wednesday it had tripled its estimate of gold in the Czech Republic's Kasperske Hory deposits, but that local bureaucracy may mean the region's riches go untapped.

"The current estimates of the geological sources of gold in Kasperske Hory have, with investigations still to be completed, been raised to 3 million ounces (100 metric tons)," TVX said in a statement.

TVX Bohemia Dulni a.s., a wholly-owned unit of Toronto-based TVX Gold, acquired a six-year exploration licence from the Czech government in 1993 for the scenic Kasperske Hory area in the Sumava mountains which border Austria and Germany.

But since then, the company which has been under attack by environmentalists, had its licence suspended by the Environment Ministry. Most recently, its exploration was halted because of opposition from local landowners.
Despite the potentially huge rewards, TVX Gold Vice Chairman John Hick said his company's patience would not last forever.
Following a vocal campaign by environmentalists and the Kasperske Hory local council, landowners in the region have refused to grant rights of access.
